Relating to goth music or people.

en: A hidden supply or fund.
A cache of valuable objects or artefacts; a trove.
To amass, usually for one's own private collection.
To save or reserve in one's mind for a future need or use.

hoard.ety:
From Middle English hord, from Old English hord (“an accumulation of valuable objects cached for preservation or future use; treasure; hoard”), from Proto-West Germanic *hoʀd, from Proto-Germanic *huzdą (“treasure; hoard”), of unknown origin, but possibly derived from Proto-Indo-European *kewdʰ- (“to conceal, hide”), thus meaning “something hidden”. Cognate with German Hort (“hoard; refuge”), Icelandic hodd (“treasure”), Latin cū̆stōs (“guard; keeper”).
For the meaning development, compare Russian сокро́вище (sokróvišče, “treasure”) related to Russian скрыва́ть (skryvátʹ, “to hide, to conceal”

ex.ja: 私の友人は私の財産だ。ですので友人を蓄えたがる私の貪欲さを見逃してください。

A source of salvation in a crisis.

ex.ja: ベビーシッターを探していると伺ったんですが。

ex.en: Tom and Mary are looking for a babysitter.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーはベビーシッターを探しています。

note.ja: baby + sitter（付き添う人）。「ベビーシッター」。

en: The work of a babysitter; the care of children in the temporary absence of their parents or guardians.

babysitting.ety: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

note.ja: babysit + -ing。「子守」。

en: A large log to burn at the back of a fire.
A reserve source or supply.
To acquire something as a backlog, or to become a backlog

backlog.ety: From back + log. 1680s; originally a large log at the back of a fire. Figurative sense from 1880s, meaning "something stored up for later use". Possibly influenced by logbook as well.

ex.en: Thanks to you, the backlog of tedious work has been completed.
ex.ja: 積み重ねた退屈な仕事がおかげさまで済んできた。

note.ja: back（後ろ）+ log（丸太）。暖炉の奥に置く大きな丸太 →「ためておくもの」→「未処理分」。

en: Of, from or pertaining to Bengal or the Bengalis.
A person from Bengal or of Bengali descent.

Bengali.ety: Equivalent to Bengal + -i. Compare Assamese বঙালী (boṅali), Bengali বাঙালি (baṅali), Hindi बंगाली (baṅgālī), Classical Persian بنگالی (bangālī).

note.ja: Bengal（ベンガル地方）+ -i。「ベンガル人・ベンガル語」。

en: A bitter brownish-yellow or greenish-yellow secretion produced by the liver, stored in the gall bladder, and discharged into the duodenum…
Bitterness of temper; ill humour; irascibility.

bile.ety:
From Middle French bile, from Latin bīlis (“bile”).
Partially displaced native English gall (“bile”), from Middle English galle, from Old English galla, ġealla (“gall, bile”).

note.ja: ラテン語 bilis（胆汁）から。胆汁が多いと怒りっぽいと考えられた →「不機嫌」。

A chemical substance derived from a biological source.

en: A small square piece of rich cake, usually made with chocolate.
A sweet bread with brown sugar and currants.

brownie.ety: From brown + -ie (diminutive suffix). In folkloric sense, originally Scots. For sense 7, compare with Dutch kabouter (“a very young female member of the scout movement”) (literally "gnome").

ex.en: You'll get brownie points if you respond quickly.
ex.ja: 反応が早ければ点数が上がります。

ex.en: You might just chalk up some brownie points.
ex.ja: あなたは多少の点数はかせげるかもしれません。

note.ja: brown + -ie。「茶色の小さなもの」→ スコットランドの小妖精 →「ブラウニー（菓子）」。

en: The body of a dead animal, especially a vertebrate or other animal having flesh.
The body of a slaughtered animal, stripped of unwanted viscera, etc.

carcass.ety: Dated from the late 13th Century C.E.; from Anglo-Norman carcois, possibly related to Old French charcois. Cognate with French carcasse. But cf. also Avestan 𐬐𐬀𐬵𐬭𐬐𐬁𐬯𐬀 (kahrkās, “vulture”), and Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (klkʾs /⁠kargās⁠/, “vulture”), whence Persian کرکس (karkas, “vulture”).

ex.en: Get your carcass out of here!
ex.ja: 出ていけ。

note.ja: フランス語 carcasse（死骸）から。語源ははっきりしない。
